Roofing in Richmond, Texas

In the city, a roofer registers and pulls a permit. A mile out, on county land, the rules change. One free call, day or night, connects you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Richmond calls.

Call (832) 662-4107 Who permits your roof

  2. Service Areas
  3. Richmond

A county seat that is smaller than its neighbors

Roofing in Richmond, TX depends on which Richmond you mean. The city is the Fort Bend County seat, a town of 11,627 people at the 2020 census. The mailing address covers far more: communities such as Pecan Grove, which counted 22,782 residents that year and sits outside any city limits.

The town itself is one of the oldest in the region. The city's history says Richmond was laid out in early 1837 by Robert Eden Handy and William Lusk, near a fort at a bend of the Brazos that gave the county its name, and it was among the first towns the Republic of Texas incorporated. Around that old core, newer subdivisions have filled the farmland along the Grand Parkway and FM 359 over the last few decades.

Houston Expert Roofers does not belong to either side of that line, and it does not roof. It is a free number with an automated assistant on the other end. You describe the roof, and the call goes through to an independent, locally owned roofing company that works in Richmond, which inspects, writes the estimate, does the job and collects payment from you.

Roof services Richmond callers need

Richmond calls tend to split by the age of the house. Older homes near the courthouse and in Pecan Grove need repairs and replacements on roofs that have been through decades of Gulf storms. Newer houses mostly call about wind damage and leaks. Each page below walks through what a careful roofer checks and the questions to ask.

Who permits a roof with a Richmond address

Three different authorities can have a say, depending on where the house sits. Your property tax statement lists the taxing units on your lot; if the City of Richmond is not one of them, you are on county land.

  • Inside the cityThe City of Richmond Building Department takes permit applications through the city's online permit portal. Its permit office is at 600 Morton Street, 281-232-6871, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Contractor registrationThe city amended its building code to require contractors working in Richmond to register, and registration is needed to pull a permit. Its notice said the process had no fee.
  • Unincorporated Fort Bend CountyCounty engineering requires a residential development permit for new structures or additions of 400 square feet or more. A plain re-roof is not on its list; ask at Permits@fbctx.gov or 281-633-7500 if unsure.
  • Your associationMost master-planned communities need architectural approval for a new roof color or material, and that holds whether or not any government permit applies.

The city's contractor registration notice dates from several years back, so confirm today's requirements with the permit office before the roofer starts. If a roofer working inside the city cannot show a Richmond registration, it cannot pull the permit itself, and that is worth knowing before you sign. Fort Bend County is inland of the Texas Department of Insurance's designated catastrophe area, so no TDI windstorm inspection applies to a Richmond roof.

The Brazos, Harvey and Beryl: what Richmond roofs have been through

The Brazos River runs right past downtown, and the weather service keeps a river gauge at Richmond. The river is a flood threat more than a roof threat, but the storms that raise it also soak every roof in town for days. These events come from the National Weather Service's river gauge record and from Fort Bend County figures reported by Community Impact.

WhenWhat happenedWhat it means for a roof
June 2, 2016The Brazos at Richmond crested at 54.74 feet, a record at the time.Days of rain find every weak pipe boot, valley and wall flashing. Leaks that started then may never have been traced.
September 1, 2017After Hurricane Harvey, the river set a new record crest of 55.19 feet at the Richmond gauge.Long rain events can saturate decking under a failing roof. A roofer should check for soft spots and stained sheathing in the attic.
May 16, 2024The derecho drove a swath of winds above 100 mph through the Houston metro, according to the National Weather Service's Houston/Galveston office.Wind breaks shingle seal strips even on houses that look fine from the yard.
July 8, 2024Hurricane Beryl brought gusts up to 94 mph in Fort Bend County. On July 9, CenterPoint's tracker showed about 59 percent of county customers still without power, and the county expected around $20 million in recovery costs.Tropical gusts lift ridge caps and drop the big pecans and oaks that shade older Richmond streets onto roofs.

If any of these storms left a stain on a ceiling that was painted over rather than traced, ask the roofer to start in the attic. Many roofers inspect at no charge; confirm that on the call.

Older Richmond, newer Richmond

Pecan Grove shows how fast the area around the city has grown. The census counted 13,551 people there in 2000 and 22,782 in 2020. Its houses span several decades of building, so a single street can mix original roofs, second roofs and recent storm replacements. Big trees are part of the appeal and part of the roofing problem: shade keeps leaves and moisture on shingles, and a heavy limb is the most common way a tropical storm punches a hole in a roof.

Farther out, communities like Harvest Green, where home sales began in 2015 according to a 2019 Houstonia feature, are young enough that many roofs are still the builder's originals. There, the first question after a leak is whether the builder's written warranty or the shingle maker's warranty applies, or whether a storm caused it and it belongs with your insurer.

The HOA step comes before the order

Associations in these communities usually review roof colors and materials. Texas Property Code section 202.011 says an association may not forbid shingles designed to resist wind and hail, or to cut energy use, so long as they resemble shingles it already allows. Send the committee the product name and color and wait for the approval letter before the roofer orders material.

Why Richmond homeowners call the line

Not sure which rules apply

City or county, permit or not, registration or not. A roofing company that takes Richmond work every week should sort that out before it writes a price, and should name the office it will deal with in the contract.

A limb on the roof after a storm

The oaks and pecans that shade older Richmond streets are the first thing tropical wind brings down. Keep everyone away from the limb and any wire it touched, report downed lines to CenterPoint Energy, and let a roofer judge the damage.

A roof older than the paperwork

Many owners in Richmond's established neighborhoods do not know how many layers are on the roof or when it last came off. A careful roofer checks the edge and the attic and tells you what it found before quoting a tear-off.

One number for any hour

Storms do not keep office hours. The line answers around the clock, and if the roofing company it reaches cannot answer, it is handed your name, number and need so it can ring you back, and you are not dialing down a list in the dark.

Stay off the roof. Wet, storm-damaged roofs are slick and the decking may be weak, so leave the ladder in the garage. Keep well away from downed power lines and report them to CenterPoint Energy or 911. Indoors, move belongings away from the leak, put a bucket or towels under the drip and keep people out of any room where the ceiling sags. Photograph the damage from the ground and inside the house, then call your insurer and a roofer.

What to ask a Richmond roofer before you sign

Rules and records

  • Is my address inside the City of Richmond, and if so, are you registered with the city?
  • Which permit will you pull, from which office, and will it be in your name?
  • Will you prepare my association's architectural submittal?
  • Can your insurer send me a certificate of liability insurance directly?

The roof

  • How many layers are on it now, and will you remove all of them?
  • What is your written price per sheet if decking is soft from old leaks?
  • Will you look in the attic for stains from past storms before you quote?
  • What written workmanship warranty do you give, and will you register the shingle warranty?

Compare estimates line by line. The roof replacement cost guide explains what moves a price, and the roof insurance claims guide covers storm claims.

How a call from Richmond works

  1. Call the numberAn automated assistant answers (832) 662-4107 at any hour and asks which service you need, since the line also takes heating, cooling, pressure washing and water damage calls.
  2. Describe the roofA leak, missing shingles, hail, a limb on the roof or an old roof you want looked at, plus your part of greater Houston and how urgent it is.
  3. Get put throughYour call is transferred to an independent, locally owned roofing company, which hears a short summary before it picks up.
  4. Deal with the roofer directlyIt inspects, quotes and does the work, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it misses the call, it gets your name, number, city and need to call you back.

The deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance says it is illegal for a contractor to offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice saying so. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a property it works on. Treat any offer to "cover the deductible" as a reason to call someone else.

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Does a roofer need to register with the City of Richmond?

Yes, for work inside the city limits. The City of Richmond amended its building code to require contractors doing business in the city to register, and its notice says registration is what lets a contractor pull building permits; it also said the process carried no fee. Ask a roofer for proof of its Richmond registration if your house is inside the city, and confirm with the permit office at 281-232-6871 whether your job needs a permit.

Is Pecan Grove part of the City of Richmond?

No. Pecan Grove is a census-designated place in Fort Bend County that sits in the extraterritorial jurisdictions of Houston and Richmond, not inside either city. At the 2020 census it had 22,782 residents, nearly twice the City of Richmond's 11,627. For a roof, that means City of Richmond permit and registration rules do not apply there, and the county's rules and your association's deed restrictions do.

Does Fort Bend County require a permit for a new roof?

The county engineering department's permit page ties its residential development permit to new structures, or additions, of 400 square feet or more on unincorporated land, and it does not list a plain shingle replacement. Rules change and floodplain lots can differ, so if you are unsure, email Permits@fbctx.gov or call 281-633-7500 before work begins. The roof replacement page covers what the job itself should include.

How do I find a roofing company in Richmond, TX I can trust?

Start with what you can verify, since Texas does not license roofers. Inside the city, ask for the City of Richmond registration. Everywhere, ask for a certificate of liability insurance mailed from the insurer, a written scope and price, and a list of Fort Bend County addresses where it replaced roofs that you can see from the street. The guide to checking a roofer covers each step.

Can I call the line at night from Richmond if a storm opens up my roof?

Yes. The automated assistant answers at any hour, sorts your call to roofing, and asks for a short account of the damage and your neighborhood before transferring you to an independent roofing company that takes Richmond calls. If the company cannot pick up, it is sent your name, number, city, need and urgency so it can call back. Until then, stay indoors, catch the drips, and see the emergency roof repair page.
